title: Motion: Displacement and Velocity
competency: Explain the difference between distance and displacement in everyday situations; distinguish between speed and velocity using the concept of vectors; and describe uniform velocity using distance-time graphs.
objectives: Interpret distance-time graphs to describe an object's motion.
Identify the reference point in a given motion scenario.
introduction: To describe how things move, we use specific scientific terms. Moving from one place to another involves a change in position relative to a reference point. In this lesson, we quantify that movement using distance, displacement, speed, and velocity.
content:
1. Distance vs. Displacement

  • Distance: The total length of the path traveled by an object. It is a scalar quantity (only magnitude).
  • Displacement: The straight-line distance between the starting point and the ending point, including direction. It is a vector quantity (magnitude and direction).

2. Speed vs. Velocity

  • Speed: How fast an object moves. Formula: Speed = Distance / Time.
  • Velocity: Speed in a specific direction. Formula: Velocity = Displacement / Time. A change in either speed or direction results in a change in velocity.

3. Graphing Motion (Distance-Time Graphs)

We use graphs to visualize motion:

  • Horizontal Line: The object is at rest (speed is zero).
  • Straight Sloping Line: The object is moving at a constant (uniform) speed.
  • Steeper Slope: Indicates higher speed.
  • Curved Line: Indicates that the speed is changing (acceleration).

examples.title: The 400m Run
examples.description: An athlete runs one full lap around a 400m circular track. The Distance traveled is 400m, but the Displacement is 0m because they returned to the starting point.

examples.title: Velocity Check
examples.description: A car traveling at 60 km/h and another car traveling at 60 km/h North have the same speed, but different velocities because one specifies direction.

keyTerms.definition: A fixed place or object used to determine if an object is in motion.
A physical quantity that has magnitude only (e.g., distance, speed).
A physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction (e.g., displacement, velocity).

keyConcepts: Motion is relative to a reference point.
Displacement is always less than or equal to distance.
The slope of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the object.
summary: Motion is described using distance and displacement. While distance tracks the whole path, displacement only cares about the start and end. Similarly, velocity adds direction to speed. These relationships can be visualized and analyzed using distance-time graphs.

selfCheck.q: If you walk 5m East and 5m West, what is your total displacement?
What does a steep slope on a distance-time graph indicate?
selfCheck.a: The object is moving fast (high speed).

selfCheck.q: Is '20 m/s South' a measure of speed or velocity?
